quizName:
DMV Practice Test  #16
										  					
  

30 Questions • Passing Score 24

questions.question: Which statement about blind spots is true?

options.text: Blind spots are eliminated if you have one outside mirror on each side.
Large trucks have bigger blind spots than most passenger vehicles.
You can check blind spots by looking in your rearview mirrors.

questions.correctAnswerText: Large trucks have bigger blind spots than most passenger vehicles.
questions.explanation: Blind spots are areas you cannot see in your mirrors. Large trucks have large blind spots. Other drivers should avoid these areas.

questions.question: At a red light with a green arrow, you may proceed in the arrow's direction if:

options.text: You first come to a complete stop.
You wait until the light changes.
You are in the correct lane and the road is clear.

questions.correctAnswerText: You are in the correct lane and the road is clear.
questions.explanation: If your lane has a green arrow signal, you may proceed in that direction when the road is clear. This is true whether the arrow appears alone or with other signals.

questions.question: As your speed increases, it is important to:

options.text: Turn on your headlights.
Look well ahead of your vehicle.
Change lanes frequently.

questions.correctAnswerText: Look well ahead of your vehicle.
questions.explanation: Your vehicle needs more distance to stop at higher speeds. Looking far ahead gives you time to react safely to hazards.

questions.question: Looking far ahead while driving on the highway:

options.text: Helps you keep up with traffic.
Reduces the need for sudden braking or turning.
Allows you to spot upcoming police officers.

questions.correctAnswerText: Reduces the need for sudden braking or turning.
questions.explanation: Watching ahead lets you see problems early. This reduces sudden braking and turning, makes driving safer, saves fuel, and keeps traffic moving smoothly.

questions.question: This sign means:

options.text: No U-turn.
No left turn.
No right turn.

questions.correctAnswerText: No right turn.
questions.explanation: This sign means you cannot turn right at this intersection. Turning right here is unsafe and against the law.

questions.question: Sudden wind gusts on highways:

options.text: Generally affect only large vehicles.
Only cause visibility problems.
Can cause problems for all vehicles.

questions.correctAnswerText: Can cause problems for all vehicles.
questions.explanation: Strong wind affects all drivers. Wind can reduce visibility by blowing dirt and dust, and it can also physically push a vehicle across the road.

questions.question: If there is a deep puddle on the road ahead, you should:

options.text: Maintain the posted speed to get through the water.
Avoid the puddle if possible.
Shift into neutral while driving through the water.

questions.correctAnswerText: Avoid the puddle if possible.
questions.explanation: Avoid slippery areas like ice, wet leaves, oil, and deep puddles to prevent skidding. Dry, solid surfaces are safest for driving.

questions.question: To improve visibility in rain or fog, use your:

options.text: Low beam headlights.
High beam headlights.
Parking lights.

questions.correctAnswerText: Low beam headlights.
questions.explanation: Use low beam headlights in rain or fog. Low beams help other drivers see you, even if they don't improve your visibility much.

questions.question: This sign means:

options.text: Curves ahead.
Divided highway starts.
Divided highway ends.

questions.correctAnswerText: Divided highway ends.
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black markings. This sign warns that the divided highway ends ahead. Be ready to change lanes or shift your position.

questions.question: If someone is passing you in a no passing zone, you should:

options.text: Pull off the road.
Maintain your speed and position.
Slow down and let the other driver return to your lane safely.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down and let the other driver return to your lane safely.
questions.explanation: Allow the passing vehicle to return to your lane easily. This helps everyone avoid hazards ahead.

questions.question: "No zones" around trucks are areas where cars:

options.text: Disappear into blind spots or are too close for the truck driver to stop and maneuver safely.
Have enough space to travel behind the truck.
Have several car lengths between them and the truck.

questions.correctAnswerText: Disappear into blind spots or are too close for the truck driver to stop and maneuver safely.
questions.explanation: "No zones" are blind spot areas around trucks and buses. They are also areas where cars are so close that they prevent the truck driver from stopping or turning safely. Being in a "No zone" greatly increases crash risk.

questions.question: When you see a flashing yellow light at an intersection, you should:

options.text: Yield to all traffic before crossing.
Stop, then enter when it is safe.
Slow down and cross carefully.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down and cross carefully.
questions.explanation: A flashing yellow light means slow down to a safe speed and proceed with caution.

questions.question: A red arrow pointing right on a traffic light means you may:

options.text: Turn right after slowing and checking for traffic.
Not turn right until the light turns green.
Turn right after coming to a complete stop.

questions.correctAnswerText: Not turn right until the light turns green.
questions.explanation: A red arrow means stop. Wait until a green light or green arrow appears. Do not turn against a red arrow.

questions.question: If the rear of your vehicle is skidding left, you should:

options.text: Not turn your steering wheel.
Turn your steering wheel left.
Turn your steering wheel right.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn your steering wheel left.
questions.explanation: If you skid on a wet or icy road, remove your foot from the accelerator, do not use the brakes, and turn the steering wheel in the direction of the skid. If you have anti-lock brakes, apply them firmly and steer straight ahead.

questions.question: Which statement about driving speed is true?

options.text: As your speed increases, the chance of death in a crash increases.
As your speed increases, you should increase your following distance.
Both of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: Both of the above.
questions.explanation: Higher speeds increase the risk of death in a crash. At speeds above 80 miles per hour, survival in a crash is unlikely. Higher speeds require longer stopping distances, so you must increase your following distance.

questions.question: When is it legal to drive around or under a railroad crossing gate?

options.text: Never.
When you can see clearly in both directions.
When the warning lights are not flashing.

questions.correctAnswerText: Never.
questions.explanation: Never go around or under a lowered gate at a railroad crossing. After the gate is raised, only cross the tracks when you can see clearly in both directions and are sure no trains are coming.

questions.question: If you approach an intersection with a blocked view to the side, you should:

options.text: Slow down and look both ways.
Keep your speed and look both ways.
Stop, then move forward slowly until you can see clearly in both directions.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop, then move forward slowly until you can see clearly in both directions.
questions.explanation: Slow down when approaching an intersection. If you cannot see cross traffic clearly, stop completely. Then move forward slowly until you can see clearly in both directions.

questions.question: What does this road sign mean?

options.text: Flagger ahead.
Turn left at the intersection.
Last turn before a toll road.

questions.correctAnswerText: Flagger ahead.
questions.explanation: Orange signs, cones, and barrels show work zone activity. Stay alert and be ready for unexpected conditions. This sign warns you that a flagger is ahead. You must obey the flagger's directions.

questions.question: If your vehicle is about to be hit from the rear, you should NOT:

options.text: Release your seat belt.
Brace yourself.
Press your head against the head restraint.

questions.correctAnswerText: Release your seat belt.
questions.explanation: When hit from the rear, your body will be thrown backward. Stay braced by pressing against your seat back and putting your head against the head restraint to prevent whiplash. Keep a firm grip on the steering wheel and be ready to apply the brakes.

questions.question: Which statement is true?

options.text: Driving too slowly is not unsafe.
Driving too slowly on certain highways can be dangerous.
Speed does not affect safety.

questions.correctAnswerText: Driving too slowly on certain highways can be dangerous.
questions.explanation: Driving too slowly is dangerous. It frustrates drivers behind you and makes them more likely to pass unsafely. Drive with the flow of traffic and stay within the speed limit.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: No U-turn.
No turning.
No left turn.

questions.correctAnswerText: No U-turn.
questions.explanation: This sign means you cannot make a U-turn. You cannot turn around to go in the opposite direction at this location.

questions.question: In very foggy conditions, you should slow down and:

options.text: Turn on your emergency flashers.
Use your high beam headlights.
Use your low beam headlights.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use your low beam headlights.
questions.explanation: Use low beams in fog, snow, rain, or mist. High beam light reflects off moisture and creates glare that makes seeing harder. Many vehicles have fog lights that work well with low beams.

questions.question: What do double solid yellow lines in the road center mean?

options.text: Passing is allowed from both directions.
Passing is allowed only from your direction.
Passing is not allowed from either direction.

questions.correctAnswerText: Passing is not allowed from either direction.
questions.explanation: Double yellow lines mean no one can cross the center line to pass, from either direction.

questions.question: You are on the freeway behind a large truck. You should drive:

options.text: Close behind the truck in bad weather because the driver can see farther ahead.
Farther behind the truck than you would behind a regular car.
One car length behind so the driver can see you.

questions.correctAnswerText: Farther behind the truck than you would behind a regular car.
questions.explanation: If you follow too closely behind a truck, the driver cannot see you in the side mirrors. Tailgating any vehicle is dangerous because you lose time to react if the vehicle stops quickly.

questions.question: When driving at night, you should:

options.text: Always use high beams.
Look directly at oncoming headlights.
Increase your following distance.

questions.correctAnswerText: Increase your following distance.
questions.explanation: Night driving is more hazardous than daytime driving because you cannot see as well. It is harder to judge speed and distance. Increase the space between you and the vehicle ahead in case they stop suddenly. Use headlights correctly, switching between high and low beams as needed.

questions.question: You exit the freeway on a downhill ramp that curves. You should:

options.text: Slow to a safe speed before entering the curve.
Slow to the freeway speed limit.
Wait until you enter the curve to start braking.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow to a safe speed before entering the curve.
questions.explanation: Always slow down before entering a curve. You cannot see what is ahead, and braking in a curve may cause your vehicle to skid.

questions.question: When driving on gravel or dirt roads:

options.text: Your tires grip better than on pavement.
Your tires have less traction than on pavement, so you must slow down.
Visibility is better than on pavement.

questions.correctAnswerText: Your tires have less traction than on pavement, so you must slow down.
questions.explanation: Gravel and dirt roads provide less traction than concrete or asphalt. You must slow down. Your vehicle will take much longer to stop and is more likely to skid when turning.

questions.question: You can cross double yellow lines to pass if the:

options.text: Vehicle in front moves right to let you pass.
Yellow line on your side of the road is broken.
Yellow line on the opposite side of the road is broken.

questions.correctAnswerText: Yellow line on your side of the road is broken.
questions.explanation: A broken yellow line means traffic on that side can pass if it is safe to do so.

questions.question: If your vehicle loses traction on wet roads, you should:

options.text: Drive at a constant speed to gain traction.
Press the brakes firmly to prevent sliding.
Slow down gradually without using the brakes.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down gradually without using the brakes.
questions.explanation: At speeds as low as 30 mph in heavy rain, your tires can lose contact with the road and ride on water. This is called hydroplaning. If this happens, slow down gradually and do not use the brakes.

questions.question: When should drivers yield to pedestrians in a crosswalk?

options.text: Only if pedestrians wave to you first.
Only if pedestrians are not texting while walking.
At all times.

questions.correctAnswerText: At all times.
questions.explanation: Stop completely at a crosswalk to let any pedestrian or vehicle in the intersection pass. You can only proceed if your lane is completely clear.
